slides.texte_overlay:
weird things your brain does
when you're stressed

it forgets simple words

stress pulls energy away from the parts of your brain that handle language. that's why you suddenly can't find an easy word in the middle of a hard conversation.

it shrinks your vision

under pressure your brain narrows your focus to the threat in front of you. you literally notice less around you, which is why you miss obvious solutions.

it replays old mistakes

a stressed brain scans the past for danger, so it digs up embarrassing memories from years ago. they feel urgent, but they're just your alarm system misfiring.

it craves something new

learning one calm new thing, like a star or a painting, gives a stressed brain a short and gentle break from playing the same old worries on repeat all day.

it makes time feel strange

stressful days fly by while single stressful moments drag on forever. your brain records more detail when it feels threatened, so seconds feel like minutes.
